findings.source_quote: ἵν᾿ ὃ τοῖς προτέροις χρόνοις οὐκ εἰργάσαντο, νῦν ἀναδράμωσιν τὰς ἡμέρας καὶ ἀγαθόν τι ποιήσωσιν.
findings.english_quote: They must now make up the days and do some good that they did not do before.
findings.issue: The source presents making up the days and doing good as the purpose of the swift repentance, using ἵνα with subjunctive verbs. The simplified edition replaces that purpose relationship with a separate explicit obligation, “They must.” This adds modal force to this clause and leaves its purpose connection unexpressed; the standard edition preserves that connection.
findings.suggested_revision: A candidate for fresh review is: “This is so they can now make up the days and do some good that they did not do before.” Preserve the connection to swift repentance rather than introducing a separate “must” statement.

summary: Both editions were reviewed clause by clause against the selected Greek working source, including its editorial supplements. The standard edition has no identified concrete fidelity defect. The simplified edition needs revision where a purpose clause becomes an independent obligation. Both retain the selected negation and repentance condition, disclose their editorial status and the reported alternatives, and follow the servant and contextual repentance policies. The supplied reports support the bounded witness disclosures; this review does not authenticate unseen manuscripts, certify editions, or establish exhaustive collation. The proposed replacement remains subject to fresh review.
